title: Multilingual website — translate your page into up to 28 languages
body:
On the **Többnyelvű honlap** card (at the bottom of the Modules tab) you can order to have your
page available in several languages. The system supports **29 languages**: the 24 official
languages of the European Union, plus Serbian, Ukrainian, Russian, Turkish and Norwegian. Your
page's own language is excluded from these (it already exists in that language), so you **choose
from 28 languages**.

The translation applies both to the texts you enter AND to the entire interface (buttons, labels).
This is how a guest switches languages:

- **On a computer:** they click the language-switcher button in the top right corner of the page,
  and choose from the drop-down list.
- **On a phone:** instead of the corner button, a **language bar running across the top of the
  page** appears, with the flags lined up next to each other — one tap, and it switches. This
  scrolls up out of view as you scroll down, so if you want to check it, scroll back to the top
  of the page.

![Screenshot: the Multilingual website card on a phone — the three package boxes, with the selectable languages by region below them](assets/hu/screen.png)

## How does it work?

1. **Choose a package** by tapping one of the three boxes at the top of the card.

   | Package | How many languages it includes |
   |---|---|
   | **Alap** | up to 3 languages |
   | **Bővített** | up to 6 languages |
   | **Teljes** | all 28 languages |

   On each box you can see the one-time fee and also how much that works out to **per language**
   — so you can compare them.
2. Then tick the languages you want. The languages are grouped by region (Neighbours, Central
   Europe, Western Europe, Southern Europe, Northern Europe, Eastern Europe). Your page's own
   language does not count, so it cannot be selected.
   - **Directly ABOVE the flag language grid** is a row that always states **how many more
     languages you can select for the same price**. On a phone the grid is long (28 languages),
     so look for this row at the top of the grid, not at the bottom. If the package is full, the
     additional languages appear dimmed and disabled — in that case you can select more by
     switching to a larger package.
   - If you choose the **Teljes** package, there is nothing to tick: instead of the list of
     languages, the card shows what is in the package — all 28 languages will be prepared.
   - If you switch back to a smaller package, the excess selections are removed, and the count
     follows immediately. Nothing disappears unnoticed.
   - **You must select at least one language** — the package cannot be bought empty. (On your
     first purchase the list opens empty, so in that case it's up to you.)
3. Important: **the translation is made from what is saved.** Before you pay, review the Texts
   tab and the module settings, and save everything — we translate what you have saved.
4. Tap the **„Fizetés és generálás”** button. You will be taken to the secure payment page; on
   the button you can see the one-time fee.
5. After payment, the card switches to the **„Kifizetve”** state: it displays the amount paid,
   the time of payment, the **reference ID**, the name of the **package** purchased
   (Alap / Bővített / Teljes) and the purchased languages. The language ticks freeze at this
   point, and the payment button is disabled with the label **„Kifizetve — nem kell újra
   fizetnie”**: the same generation cannot be bought twice.
6. The translation is ready within a few minutes, and the language versions appear on your page
   by themselves. Links to them appear on the card, and the button becomes active again — from
   then on with the label **„Újragenerálás fizetéssel”**.

⚠️ **After payment the three package boxes and the capacity row disappear from the card**, and
the language ticks freeze. This is not an error: while the paid translation is being prepared,
there is nothing to select. As soon as it is done, the selection opens up again — and then you
can also choose a different package.

## I paid, but the card still shows that it's being prepared

This is fine: the translation takes a few minutes. If it takes longer than expected, the system
**restarts it by itself** within a few minutes — the card even states this, and shows which
attempt we are on. **You do not need to pay again** in this case either, and the button won't
allow it: we have received the fee, the work is on our side.

If it does not succeed even after several automatic attempts, the card will state this too, and
one of our colleagues will **contact you on their own initiative** — you don't need to chase it
up yourself. If you do write to us anyway, please quote the **reference ID** on the card.

## What if the payment is declined?

No charge is made — the page after payment states this. On this same page (this is already the
return from the payment provider, not the interface) you can restart the same order with one
button, and you will also find the reference ID there, which it is worth quoting if you write
to us.

## What happens if I modify my texts later?

Your own-language page updates immediately, free of charge — just as before. The translated
versions, however, **do not update by themselves**: they continue to show the last paid state.
In that case a warning appears on the card that the translations are out of date, and we also
send an email about it. If you want the translations to show the fresh text too, start the
regeneration — this again costs the one-time generation fee.

## Can I swap a language?

Yes. When regenerating you simply tick different languages — and you can even choose a different
package. With the new payment the old language version is removed, and the new languages are
generated. The most recently paid language set is always the active one.

## How much does it cost?

On the box of the selected package, and in the **„Egyszeri díj”** row at the bottom of the card,
you always see the current price — on a phone this row stays at the bottom of the screen, so you
can see what you are paying even while selecting. Every generation — the first one, the
regeneration and the language swap too — costs the package price. **This module has no monthly
fee.**

If you have a valid introductory discount, on the boxes you see the list price struck through
and, next to it, the amount you actually pay.
